evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫 (CUHK Multi-function Chinese Character Database)
evidence.field: 形義通解; 毛 entry, lines 142–146
evidence.text: The entry interprets 毛 as a pictograph of human hair and animal hair or feathers. It describes Zhou bronze forms as hair, sometimes with a dot beneath the vertical stroke as decoration, and reports that the dot appears as a short horizontal stroke in some Warring States Chu forms. It also reports bronze uses as a state or lineage name, a personal name, and as 毛 read for 旄, an ox-tail standard ornament. Its proposed extension to ‘fine, minute’ from the smallness of hairs is an analysis, not a dated semantic sequence.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫

evidence.source: Academia Sinica, International Encoding for Chinese Characters and Variants Knowledge Base
evidence.text: The character page identifies 毛 as U+6BDB and lists a bronze example indexed as 集成04009, Chu manuscript forms, and a small-seal form associated with Shuowen. It supplies period/form labels, but not a textual description of individual glyph shapes; it does not by itself establish the earliest attestation of the spoken word.
evidence.title: 漢字「毛」：字形演變

evidence.source: Shuowen.org, online text of 說文解字
evidence.text: The entry gives the Shuowen analysis 象形 and the definition concerning eyebrows, hair, and animal hair. This is a historical lexicographic account, not direct proof of the graph's original depicted referent.
evidence.title: 說文解字「毛」

gaps: No secure dated earliest attestation of 毛 meaning hair, fur, or feather was established. CUHK documents bronze graphic examples but reports some early inscriptions as names or a 毛-for-旄 use; the accessible evidence does not securely date the common noun sense.

The exact character's early glyph sequence is incompletely documented in accessible text: Academia Sinica lists bronze, Chu manuscript, and small-seal stages, and CUHK describes some bronze and Chu features, but no first-attested shape or graphic corruption was established. No inspected evidence confirms an oracle-bone form.

The graph's depicted referent is disputed or broad: the dossier's Dong Chinese note says feather; Shuowen says eyebrows, hair, and animal hair; CUHK describes human/animal hair and feathers. The evidence does not isolate one original depicted object, species, or precise referent.
CUHK's fine/minute semantic extension from small hairs is an undated proposed path. Other senses are not chronologically ordered; dictionary gloss lists were not treated as chronology.

CUHK reports 毛 used as 旄 in a bronze inscription for a standard ornament, but independent early attestations and historical pronunciation of the underlying ornament word were not established. This is a reported whole-graph loan, not evidence of a sound component within 毛.
The dossier's Proto-Sino-Tibetan cognate proposal was not independently tested against primary comparative lexical sources in this pass.

The official Unicode per-character URL https://www.unicode.org/cgi-bin/GetUnihanData.pl?codepoint=6BDB could not be opened. A secondary Unihan-derived character record reports kMandarin máo, but it does not satisfy the required official click-through evidence.

No local-source permission review or extract recommendation: the recurring paleographic evidence is concise and character-specific, and the inspected sources do not provide a clearly verified bulk-reuse permission for their dictionary text. No extract is recommended.

The Commons description page search result gave its identity and public-domain status, but direct page opens returned cache-miss errors. No actual pixels were inspected; the harness visual agent should confirm the redraw's appearance and educational fit.

Academia Sinica's 毛 evolution record provides bronze, Chu manuscript, and seal-stage labels, but that specific database page is marked all rights reserved; Xiaoxuetang query images have a CC0 notice, but no specific Xiaoxuetang 毛 image was selected or inspected as an alternative.
